name: Reactive Ball Chaser
description: Ball-centric, reactive. Constantly drives straight toward the current ball_position and applies force in the direction of (ball_position - ego_agent_position) clipped by a maximum thrust. If within a close capture radius, orient pushes to drive the ball toward goal_positions by applying force in direction (goal_positions - ego_agent_position). Use short-range repulsion from teammate_position and nearby adversary_positions to avoid physical blocking: if another agent is within a small safety radius, add a small lateral force away from that agent. This policy does not predict future trajectories — it reacts to observed positions and velocities only. Practical pseudocode: compute target = ball_position; if dist(ego, ball) < capture_radius then target = goal_positions; desired = normalize(target - ego_agent_position) * max_force; avoid = sum_{p in nearby_agents} k_repulse * (ego - p)/dist^2; action = clip(desired + avoid). Output as torch tensor shape (1,2).

name: Anticipatory Ball Interceptor
description: Ball-centric, proactive. Predicts where the ball (and likely opponent interceptors) will be after a short time horizon and moves to an interception point rather than the current ball_position. Estimate t_intercept from relative distance and a nominal travel speed: intercept_point = ball_position + ball_velocity * t_intercept. If an adversary is closer to that intercept_point (using distance + their velocity direction), and teammate is farther, choose an alternate interception point slightly biased toward the goal to cut off opponent clearance. If teammate_position is already converging on the same intercept_point (teammate closer), yield by switching to a supporting intercept: move to a secondary intercept point that opens a passing lane (between the ball predicted path and goal_positions). Also maintain collision avoidance and small defensive fallback: if the ball is on our defensive half, prioritize blocking opponent approach lines. Implementation hint: compute predicted ball_pos = ball_position + ball_velocity * t; choose t that minimizes |ego_agent_position - predicted_ball_pos|/ego_speed. Produce force toward chosen interception point (normalize and scale), with small repulsive terms from nearby agents. Output as torch tensor (1,2).

name: Reactive Support / Zone Maintainer
description: Off-ball, reactive support. Focuses on maintaining a useful position relative to the ball and goal without predicting far into the future. Primary rule: place yourself in the open space between the ball and the opponent goal but offset laterally to create a passing angle. If teammate is closer to the ball, move forward to an offering position: compute desired = interpolate(ball_position, goal_positions, alpha) then add a perpendicular offset away from nearest defender to remain open. If the ball is in our defensive half or an opponent is advancing toward our goal, drop back to a central blocking position between ball and our goal_positions. Use only current positions and velocities to decide swaps: if teammate_position is within a close contest distance of the ball, increase distance to avoid collision; otherwise close in to present a pass option. Action = force toward desired position with small velocity damping to hold zone, output as torch tensor (1,2).

name: Proactive Space Creator / Lead Runner
description: Off-ball, proactive. Attempts to create and exploit future space based on teammate_velocity and adversary_positions. Predict teammate intent from teammate_velocity (direction of attack) and run ahead into channels that will open: compute a lead_point = teammate_position + normalize(teammate_velocity) * lead_distance, then shift lead_point laterally to exploit gaps between adversary_positions (choose the lateral offset that maximizes distance from the nearest defender). If adversaries are converging on the teammate, instead cut behind their line of motion to receive a through pass (compute defender_line from pairs of adversary_positions and aim to run into the space behind that line). If the predicted channel is likely blocked (closest defender to lead_point is nearer than ego), revert to drawing defenders by running wide or deep to pull them away. Use prediction horizons (ball_velocity and teammate_velocity) to time the run; if a pass window is predicted, accelerate toward lead_point; otherwise maintain a distractor run to create space. Action is directed force toward chosen lead_point with additional short-range avoidance; return as torch tensor (1,2).
